summary: The project is a web app aimed at visualizing the burning across the world. While people are aware of the fact that there is a fire, they are often unaware of the exact region, cause, fire path, and frequency of hotspots in that region over multiple years. They can also visualize how these visualizations change over time with a play feature. For those unable to view trends, there are accessibility options such as speaking and listening to the trends.
details: This project creates a dashboard for users to be able to visualize burning across the world. The first step is to upload any files of the Modis or VIIRS data across any region and any timeframe. then the platform automatically filters the countries in the country tab to those contained in the files uploaded. You can then click on a country to visualize trends across that specific country, or just view trends across all countries visualized in the files. You can then determine how you want to see the map, how you want the map to be colored, and also if you need any accessibility options such as colorblind accessibility on the map or using audio to explain the map to the user. The user can also alternatively use the voice option to explain what they want to see rather than use the dropdown menus. You can then choose to see the Calendar, trends, fire path, and correlations between the different burning spots. At the top you will also see metrics such as hotspots in view, most active month, most active year, standard duration, etc. This project is creative because it allows the user to learn more about hotspots and burning, through the method that they find best. Many users know about fire events, but they are unable to understand future fire paths, patterns, trends, and other specificities. This website will allow for users to see past trends and potentially predict fire paths and consequences, informing and alerting them ahead of time. With more data, I want to implement a predict feature that would allow users to visualize how a fire path might develop in the future, allowing them to be alerted. Javascript was used for this project along with HTML and CSS for design components.
